nodes.summary: For contexts $\Gamma$, $\Delta$ and $\Xi$, a renaming $\rho$ from $\Gamma$ to $\Delta$ and a renaming $\sigma$ from $\Delta$ to $\Xi$, the composite of $\rho$ followed by $\sigma$ is the renaming from $\Gamma$ to $\Xi$ that sends each variable $x$ to $\sigma(\rho(x))$.

nodes.summary: For every simultaneous substitution $\sigma$ from a context $\Gamma$ to a context $\Delta$ and every variable $x$ of type $A$ in $\Gamma$, the composite of $\sigma$ followed by the identity substitution on $\Delta$ sends $x$ to $\sigma(x)$.

nodes.title: Composing a single substitution with a substitution

nodes.summary: For substitutions $\sigma$ from a context $\Gamma$ to $\Delta$ and $\tau$ from $\Delta$ to $\Xi$, the composite of $\sigma$ followed by $\tau$ is the substitution from $\Gamma$ to $\Xi$ that sends each variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to the term obtained by applying $\tau$ to $\sigma(x)$.
nodes.title: Composition of simply typed substitutions

nodes.summary: Given a term $a$ of type $A$ in a context $\Delta$ and a substitution $\sigma$ from $\Gamma$ to $\Delta$, the extension of $\sigma$ by $a$ is the substitution from the context $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$ to $\Delta$ that sends the newest variable to $a$ and each older variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to $\sigma(x)$.

nodes.title: Identity substitution (simply typed lambda calculus)

nodes.summary: Let $b$ be a term of type $B$ in the context $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$, and $a$ a term of type $A$ in $\Gamma$. Instantiating the newest variable of $b$ by $a$ gives the same term as applying to $b$ the substitution that sends the newest variable to $a$ and each older variable to itself, that is, the extension of the identity substitution on $\Gamma$ by $a$.

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be a renaming from a context $\Gamma$ to a context $\Delta$ and let $A$ be a simple type, and write $A :: \Gamma$ for the context obtained by prepending $A$ to $\Gamma$. nodes.summary: For contexts $\Gamma$ and $\Delta$ and a type-preserving renaming $\rho$ from $\Gamma$ to $\Delta$, the induced substitution from $\Gamma$ to $\Delta$ sends each variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to the term consisting of the variable $\rho(x)$ alone.

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be a renaming from $\Gamma$ to $\Delta$, $b$ a term of type $B$ in the context $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$, and $a$ a term of type $A$ in $\Gamma$. Renaming by $\rho$ the instantiation of the newest variable of $b$ by $a$ gives the instantiation of the newest variable of $b'$ by $a'$, where $b'$ is $b$ renamed by the lift of $\rho$ under the binder and $a'$ is $a$ renamed by $\rho$.

nodes.title: Lifting commutes with renaming substitution images

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a substitution from $\Gamma$ to $\Delta$, $\rho$ a renaming from $\Delta$ to $\Xi$ and $t$ a term of type $A$ in $\Gamma$. Renaming by $\rho$ the result of applying $\sigma$ to $t$ gives the result of applying to $t$ the substitution that sends each variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to $\sigma(x)$ renamed by $\rho$.
nodes.title: Renaming after substitution in the simply typed calculus

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be a renaming from the typing context $\Gamma$ to the typing context $\Delta$, $t$ a term of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, and $B$ a type. Weakening $t$ by a new newest variable of type $B$ and then renaming by the lift of $\rho$ under that variable gives the same term as renaming $t$ by $\rho$ and then weakening by a new newest variable of type $B$.

nodes.summary: Given a substitution $\sigma$ from the typing context $\Gamma$ to the typing context $\Delta$ and a renaming $\rho$ from $\Delta$ to the typing context $\Xi$, the substitution from $\Gamma$ to $\Xi$ obtained by renaming images sends each variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to the renaming of the term $\sigma(x)$ by $\rho$.

Given a term $a$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, the single-variable substitution for $a$ is the substitution from $A :: \Gamma$ to $\Gamma$ that sends the newest variable to $a$ and sends the successor of each variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to the term consisting of the variable $x$ alone.

Weakening $t$ by a new newest variable of type $B$ and then applying the lift of $\sigma$ under that variable gives the same term as applying $\sigma$ to $t$ and then weakening by a new newest variable of type $B$.

Renaming $t$ by $\rho$ and then applying $\sigma$ gives the same term as applying to $t$ the substitution that sends each variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to $\sigma(\rho(x))$.

The terms of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ are generated by three rules: every variable of type $A$ in $\Gamma$ is a term of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$; if $f$ is a term of type…
nodes.title: Intrinsically typed terms of the simply typed lambda calculus

nodes.summary: Given a type $B$ of base types, the simple types over $B$ are generated by two rules: every base type $b \in B$ is a simple type, and for simple types $A$ and $C$ the function type $A \Rightarrow C$ is a simple type.
nodes.title: Simple types

nodes.summary: For a context $\Gamma$ (a list of simple types) and a simple type $A$, the variables of type $A$ in $\Gamma$ are generated by two rules: the variable $0$ is a variable of type $A$ in the context $A :: \Gamma$ obtained by prepending $A$ to $\Gamma$, and if $x$ is a variable of type $A$ in $\Gamma$, then for every simple type $B$ the successor of $x$ is a variable of type $A$ in $B :: \Gamma$.
nodes.title: Typed de Bruijn variables of the simply typed lambda calculus

nodes.summary: For a term $t$ of type $A$ in a context $\Gamma$ and a simple type $B$, write $B :: \Gamma$ for the context obtained by prepending $B$ to $\Gamma$. The weakening of $t$ is the term of type $A$ in the context $B :: \Gamma$ obtained by renaming $t$ along the renaming that sends each variable of $\Gamma$ to its successor in $B :: \Gamma$.

Computer Science

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
